headline: CBA's Loan impairment expense (LIE) fell from $2,518m in FY20 to $554m in FY21, a decrease of $1,964m or 78% (cash basis). The loan loss rate (LIE as % of average gross loans and acceptances, GLAAs) fell 26 bps to 7 bps from 33 bps. The results book's provision-type bridge sums exactly to the movement: net collective provision funding fell $1,756m (2,043→287), net new and increased individual provisioning fell $162m (658→496), and write-backs of individually assessed provisions moved $46m ((183)→(229)). The bank attributes the fall to an improvement in economic conditions and outlook. The results presentation corroborates LIE of $554m, down 78.0% on FY20, and the FY20 book confirms the $2,518m comparator and 33 bps loss rate.

drivers.narrative: Net collective provision funding fell $1,756m (2,043→287). The bank attributes the divisional decreases to lower collective provision charges reflecting an improvement in economic conditions and outlook: Retail -$900m to $134m (also reduced consumer finance balances), Business -$551m to $233m, New Zealand -$297m to a $5m benefit, Institutional -$257m to $96m. Partly offset by Corporate Centre +$41m to $96m on higher collective charges in PTBC (Indonesia COVID-19 deterioration).

drivers.bank_label: Net new and increased individual provisioning
drivers.narrative: Net new and increased individual provisioning fell $162m (658→496). The bank cites lower individual provisions in the current year as a driver within the New Zealand and Institutional Banking and Markets decreases, alongside their lower collective charges.

Write-backs of individually assessed provisions increased from $183m to $229m, contributing -$46m to the charge. The bank does not disclose a specific reason for this component beyond the overall improvement in economic conditions and outlook.

notable_items: Corporate Centre and Other LIE increased $41m to $96m on higher collective provision charges in PTBC (Indonesia COVID-19 deterioration) - the only division to rise
limitations: The provision-type bridge (page 126) is the canonical driver table and sums exactly to the -$1,964m movement; residual is zero.
The divisional where-layer (page 39) also sums to -$1,964m; divisional deltas are attributed to the collective driver per the bank's prose, with individual provisions cited for NZ and Institutional.
The bank does not disclose a specific reason for the write-back component beyond the overall improvement in economic conditions and outlook.

The FY20 comparator of $2,518m is confirmed by the FY20 results book (page 39); the FY21 book's restated division names (Business Banking, Corporate Centre and Other) replace the FY20 book's (Business and Private Banking, IFS and other).

Capped at 80: collective -1756 $m, individual_provisions -162 $m, write_backs_recoveries -46 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
